labelChirho: opener of (the womb), that which opens
descriptionChirho: Active participial noun פֶּטֶר in construct with רֶחֶם 'womb,' denoting literally 'that which opens the womb,' i.e., the first issue of the womb. Used in legal-cultic contexts prescribing consecration of firstborn animals and humans (Ex 13:12, 13:15, 34:19; Num 18:15). Multilingual evidence reflects the literal active sense: eng: opener-of, spa: que-abre, hin: जो–खोलता–है, arb: فَاتِحَ, kor: 여는, swa: wanaofungua.

Extended or interpretive sense of פֶּטֶר where the word is rendered not as 'opener' but directly as 'firstborn,' emphasizing the status of the offspring rather than the act of opening (Ex 13:2, Num 3:12, 8:16, Ezek 20:26). Translations shift from active verbal imagery to a status noun: eng: firstborn-of, spa: primogénito-de, hin: पहलौठा, swa: mzaliwa-wa-kwanza-wa. This semantic extension from physical act to social-legal status justifies a separate sense.
